title: Space Launch - Orbital Temple
heading: Space Launch
intro: On January 12, 2026, the Orbital Temple was aboard ISRO's PSLV-C62 rocket. The rocket lifted off and reached space, but failed in its final stage. The Orbital Temple was in space for only 10 minutes before the rocket lost control and burned up in the atmosphere.

status.heading: What happens now
status.paragraph1: A second Orbital Temple is cleared to fly on SpaceX's Transporter-18 mission from Vandenberg, California, scheduled for Thursday, October 1, 2026 at 2:18 PM New York time (18:18 UTC).
status.paragraph2: Temples take time to build. Some took centuries. The Orbital Temple carries the names of those who believed in it, and that commitment remains. We are trying again.

partnership: The first Orbital Temple launch was a partnership between NewSpace India Limited (NSIL), a Government of India Company under Department of Space, Antrix Corporation, and the artist. This collaboration represented a significant milestone for art in space exploration, bringing together India's space program with an artistic vision of radical inclusivity. The second launch is on SpaceX's Transporter-18.
